meta.format: rows[]: {fn, case?, in:{name:value}, out:{name:value}} or {fn, case?, in, revert:code}. Numbers are decimal strings; seed is a 0x-prefixed 32-byte big-endian hex string; pairing out.perm is a list of decimal strings (coin indexes of the alive set in shuffled order, empty when alive_mask is 0). Function names are the Rust engine names: pool_factor_wad, power, win_prob_bps, pairing, clash_roll, hunt_roll, plus element_bps and level_from_xp. power also returns the pool_factor_wad it used, win_prob_bps also returns power_a and power_b, for debugging. Params in every row mirror CombatMath.Params (gamma_bps, pool_factor_min_bps, pool_factor_max_bps, level_bonus_bps, element_up_bps, element_down_bps, win_prob_min_bps, win_prob_max_bps); power rows carry only the six that power reads. Production defaults: 8800, 1000, 100000, 400, 11500, 8700, 1500, 8500. revert codes: overflow (Solidity panic 0x11, arithmetic overflow or underflow, including uint8 level - 1 when level is 0 and uint8 monsterType + 1 when 255), exp_overflow (Solady ExpOverflow from powWad when ln(ratio) * gamma exceeds about 135.3 in WAD), safecast_uint_to_int (ratio >= 2^255, OpenZeppelin SafeCast).
meta.authority: outputs come from forge running contracts/src/libs/CombatMath.sol (Solady powWad, OpenZeppelin SafeCast) through near-parity/forge/script/GenCombat.s.sol

cross_check.note: shared/src has no combat math (fixtureBuilder uses its own simplified formula), so rows are verified by an independent re-implementation in gen/combat.ts; the generator fails on the first mismatch
cross_check.exact: element_bps, level_from_xp, power (from the reported pool factor), win_prob_bps (from the reported powers), pairing (keccak256 of 96 bytes via viem), clash_roll, hunt_roll are bit-exact
cross_check.pool_factor_wad: 1559 unclamped rows compared with Math.pow double precision (tolerance max(1e-11 relative, 4 wad units)); max relative diff 3.73e-16, max absolute diff 3072.0 wad; 1624 clamped rows checked for the correct branch; degenerate branches (sum 0, n 0, rLock 0, ratio 0) are exact

rust_notes: pairing/clash_roll/hunt_roll hash input is exactly 96 bytes: seed (32 bytes) || tag right-padded with zero bytes to 32 (ASCII PAIR, CLASH, HUNT) || index as 32-byte big-endian. clash_roll = hash mod 10000, hunt_roll = hash mod 100, both on the full 256-bit hash read as big-endian.

pairing: perm starts as the ascending indexes of the set bits of alive_mask (bits 0..31); then for i = n down to 2: idx = i - 1, j = hash(seed, PAIR, idx) mod i, swap perm[idx] and perm[j]. The hash index is idx (i - 1), not i.

pool_factor_wad branch order: sum_r == 0 or n == 0 returns WAD clamped to [min, max] before anything else (even when r_lock is 0); then r_lock == 0 returns min; then ratio = r_lock * n * WAD / sum_r (floor, 256-bit intermediate); ratio == 0 returns min; else raw = powWad(ratio, gamma_bps * WAD / BPS) clamped to [min_wad, max_wad] where min_wad = min_bps * WAD / BPS. min > max is not rejected: min wins below, max wins above, so min is returned when raw < min and max when raw > max.

powWad(x, y) = expWad(lnWad(x) * y / 1e18) in signed 256-bit; the division truncates toward zero (ln is negative when ratio < 1). expWad returns 0 below about -41.4 and reverts ExpOverflow at or above about 135.3 (WAD). With production gamma 8800 ExpOverflow is unreachable because ratio >= 2^255 already reverts SafeCast first.

power = pool_factor_wad * (10000 + level_bonus_bps * (level - 1)) * element_bps * 10000 / 10^12. Intermediate can reach about 7e46 with extreme params (more than u128 max 3.4e38), production params stay below 2e31; use a 256-bit intermediate.

level is uint8: level == 0 reverts (checked level - 1). monster_type 255 reverts in element_bps (uint8 + 1). Types 5..254 are accepted and follow the modulo-5 rule literally, so only type pairs congruent per (a + 1) % 5 == b get the bonus; the game only uses 0..4.

win_prob_bps: bps = power_a + power_b == 0 ? 5000 : power_a * 10000 / (power_a + power_b) (floor), then clamped to [win_prob_min_bps, win_prob_max_bps], min checked first. Zero power needs pool_factor_min_bps == 0 and r_lock == 0.
level_from_xp thresholds: 15, 35, 60, 90, 125, 165, 210, 260, 320 give levels 2 to 10; every xp value up to 2^256 - 1 is accepted.
meta.pool_factor_wad_parity_note: Only Solady powWad itself is not re-derivable here: the Rust port is bit-exact with these rows only if it reproduces Solady lnWad and expWad exactly; otherwise it is within about 1e-9 relative and must be stated as such
